t: Equal Sum Arrays With Minimum Number of Operations: Greedy Gain Spending
o: All values lie in 1..6, so rewriting one element moves the sum difference by at most 5. Normalize by swapping so nums1 has the larger sum; then each element offers a maximum gain: v - 1 from the heavy array (drop toward 1) and 6 - v from the light array (raise toward 6). Minimizing operations means covering diff = sum1 - sum2 with as few gains as possible, so spend the largest gains first. Example 1 covers diff 11 with three gains of 5; example 3 likewise needs 3 ops. Example 2 (seven 1s versus one 6) has zero available gain, hence -1.
k: Swap arrays first so the gain formulas are uniform: v-1 on the heavy side, 6-v on the light side.
Impossible exactly when total available gain is below diff - e.g., a heavy array pinned at all 1s facing a light array pinned at 6.
Gains take only six values {0..5}, so bucket counting replaces sorting for a linear-time greedy.

a.i: Collect the unit-gain of every element - v-1 from the heavy array, 6-v from the light - and sort descending. Sweep through the gains subtracting from diff until it reaches 0; the number consumed is the answer. Since one operation captures an element full gain at once, taking largest gains first is optimal.
s: Swap arrays so sum(nums1) >= sum(nums2); set diff to the difference.
Build the gains list: v-1 for nums1 elements, 6-v for nums2 elements.
Sort gains descending and consume until cumulative gain >= diff.
Count consumed operations; if supply runs out first return -1.
a.t: O((n+m)*log(n+m)) - collecting gains is linear, the sort dominates

a.i: Gains take only six values, so bucket-count how many elements offer each gain g in 0..5 and process buckets from 5 downward. Within a bucket, either the whole bucket is consumed or the remaining diff is covered by ceil(diff/g) more elements - whichever comes first. This removes the sort entirely and answers in linear time.
s: Swap so nums1 is heavier; diff = sum1 - sum2.
Bucket cnt[g]: increment g = v-1 for nums1 values, g = 6-v for nums2 values.
For g = 5 down to 1: if g*cnt[g] < diff, consume the whole bucket and continue; otherwise add ceil(diff/g) operations and finish.
Return -1 if diff remains positive after all buckets.
a.t: O(n+m) - one bucketing pass plus six constant bucket sweeps

w: Lead with approach 2; fall back to sorting when you want minimal code. Pitfalls: skipping the swap (gain formulas silently invert), handling equal sums (answer 0 falls out naturally since diff starts at 0), and the impossibility case (example 2: heavy array stuck at 1s, light array stuck at 6). Note each operation may change ANY element of EITHER array to any value in 1..6 - the greedy exploits exactly that freedom. Follow-up: generalize the value range to lo..hi; the same greedy works with hi-lo gain buckets.
